aggregateDillonSentVoice.scope: globally deduplicated sent-message evidence from the 17 active client queries; revive-systems excluded
aggregateDillonSentVoice.openings: Hi is the dominant client-service opening; Hey rises with established, informal relationships. Delivery notes often move directly from greeting to the result or attachment. Formal time-of-day greetings are uncommon.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.sentenceRhythm: Typical rhythm is short greeting, clear result, grouped facts or KPI bullets, interpretation, then one next action. Brief acknowledgements can be a single sentence or a reaction; complex handoffs become longer checklist-style paragraphs.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.directness: Dillon usually leads with what is live, finished, paused, changed, or needed. He distinguishes verified metrics from modeled or inferred outcomes when the underlying evidence has been reconciled.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.warmth: The voice is appreciative, encouraging, and celebratory. Thanks, positive reinforcement, exclamation marks, and lightweight emoji reactions are common, especially after client approval or a lead win.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.asks: The strongest asks are concrete and singular: confirm a budget, review an asset, provide access, choose a direction, supply a link, or report lead quality. The ask usually follows enough context for the recipient to act immediately.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.followUps: Follow-ups restate the current state, owner, constraint, and next checkpoint. When access or source data is missing, Dillon often keeps work paused and explains what evidence will unlock the next step.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.closings: Longer messages commonly close with thanks and the DM or Dillon Mohr Marketing Specialist signature. Short thread acknowledgements may close without a full sign-off or use a Gmail reaction.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.punctuation: Exclamation marks are frequent and questions are comparatively selective. KPI and handoff messages use bullets, colons, parentheses, and dash-style separators; casual threads contain more contractions and conversational punctuation.
aggregateDillonSentVoice.revisionTendencies: Dillon replaces stale attachments, marks duplicate or stale drafts explicitly, corrects source-of-truth errors, and rewrites broad claims after verification. Revised drafts sometimes remain unsent, so Draft versus Sent status must always be preserved.
antiPatterns: Do not promote a Draft as a delivered commitment or decision.
Watch for a later internal correction that conflicts with an earlier sent message, especially channel recommendations or KPI attribution.
Avoid duplicate, stale, test, or do-not-send artifacts even when they are newer than the live thread.
Avoid blending clients, brands, cities, or verified and modeled metrics in one conclusion.
Keep personal explanations, typos, repeated signatures, and reaction-only messages out of formal client-history summaries.
Verify source and math before repeating a confident performance claim.
